kids.t: Drag this if the aircraft feels floaty or too heavy. Right makes it heavier, so it drops when you chop the throttle and stops hanging at the top of a jump. Left makes it lighter and it floats. Hover moves up and down the stick with it, which is most of what you will feel.

attrs: Weight, how heavy the quad feels

kids.t: Realistic drone combat, inspired by Paraguay's landscapes. A work in progress.
Tracks you build stay in this browser. Clearing it, or another device, starts you from nothing. Publish a track to put it on the public board.
A quad has no brakes and no wings. Point it where you want to go and push. Two minutes and you will be through a gate.
Arrow keys move, Enter selects. A radio banks the quad. Any switch selects.

A quad has no brakes and no wings. Throttle only sets how hard the props push, so the way to slow down or turn is to point the quad somewhere else and push. Fly the pulsing gate: green is the way through, red is its wrong face.
Press the keys. These follow your hands.
Throttle. Tap for a nudge, hold to climb, long hold to punch. Let go and it holds height.
Yaw, left and right on the spot.
Pitch. Forward is stick forward, nose down, fly forward.
Launch control, if you turned it on in Quad. Pitch, centre, punch.
Back to the start line, and pause.
If you end up inverted on the ground, a TURTLE MODE prompt appears. Pitch or roll with the arrow keys to flip over. You do not have to time it. Let go, then take off.
Report a bug or give feedback. Pauses if you are in the air, then opens the form.

Keys are on or off, so hold time is the analog: a tap moves the stick a little, a hold sits at a flyable amount, a long hold goes to full. Keyboard flight is Angle, so letting go brings the quad back to level.
Goes back. Arrow keys still move the menu.

How far the sticks go. Pick the rate system you think in and type your own numbers: all five of the firmware's are here and the quad flies whichever you choose. Rates belong to you, not to the tune, so they stay put when you switch tunes. A radio in Acro flies this curve; keyboard flight is Angle and ignores it.
How far the surfaces move at full stick, as the manual sets the radio up. Changes fly at once.
Goes back. Changes are already stored. Arrow keys still move the menu.

How hard the flight controller works. The sliders are the firmware's own and the firmware applies them, and they adjust the tune you have loaded: 100 is that tune's stock, the master multiplier scales everything at once. Each tune keeps its own adjustment. Rates live on their own screen and are untouched by anything here.
Choose the key and the pad button for each flight action. Press a row, then the key or the button; Escape cancels, Backspace puts the defaults back.

Pick what is in your hands and the game sets up for it. You can change it any time in the Hangar.
Arrow keys move, Enter chooses. Escape skips. On a radio: pitch to move, roll right to choose.
